acip: DE LTAR SDIG PA THAMS CAD LAS RNAM PAR GROL BAR BYED CING, LUS TE RGYUD DAG PA LAS SKYON MED PA'I MI'I MCHOG KUN NAS GTZANG SBRA'I SPYOD PA BYED PA DE, SDIG PA STE SGRIB PA THAMS CAD RNAM PAR DAG PA'I DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA RDO RJE 'CHANG GI SA 'THOB PAR 'GYUR RO,,
wylie: de ltar sdig pa thams cad las rnam par grol bar byed cing, lus te rgyud dag pa las skyon med pa'i mi'i mchog kun nas gtsang sbra'i spyod pa byed pa de, sdig pa ste sgrib pa thams cad rnam par dag pa'i de bzhin gshegs pa rdo rje 'chang gi sa 'thob par 'gyur ro
english: They too are, in the same way, liberated from all their own bad deeds; their body--which is to say, their mindstream--becomes completely pure.  They then become the immaculate Lord of All Beings, engaging in His own form of purity.  That is, they achieve the state of the One Gone Thus, the Keeper of the Diamond, free of every "bad deed," here meaning "obstacle." * * * On the need for an actual, physical partner, Choney Lama (writing in the 17th century) mentions a disagreement on the matter and expresses his own opinion in the Lamp that Illuminates the Essence: An Explanation of Critical Points in the "Harvest of Attainments" [of Je Tsongkapa], itself a Treatise on the Great, Deep Practice of the Stage of Completion, according to the System of that Great and Accomplished Saint, Luhipa (ACIP digital text S00299, ff. 35b-36a):
